photographs.alt: Top: “I is for INKWELL” in large outlined letters. Bottom left reads: “I is for...INKWELL! This small inkwell is from the archeology collection at the Abiel Smith School, which was a school for Black children in Boston from 1835 to 1855. The conditions in the school were not as good as conditions in white schools, and many people fought against this injustice. In 1855, the school closed when the state of Massachusetts outlawed separate schools for white and Black children. The outside of this inkwell is made of a soft metal called pewter and the inside is made of glass. It would have fit right into a students desk! Today, the Abiel Smith School is part of the Museum of African American History, a partner of Boston African American National Historic site.” Bottom right corner: “9”. In the center is an outline inkwell and pen. The inkwell shaped like a bucket with a flat lip at the top. Half of a broken lid to the inkwell rests across the top. There is a ink pen drawn at a downward angle in front of inkwell.
photographs.caption: I is for INKWELL
